The main thread is waiting for the physics thread to finish:

```
ConditionVariable::wait<MutexImplstd::mutex>(...)
...
CommandQueueMT::sync()
PhysicsServer3DWrapMT::sync()
Main::iteration()
...
WinMain(...)
```

and

```
ConditionVariable::wait<MutexImpl<std::mutex>>(...)
...
BetsyCompressor::_thread_loop()
call_with_variant_args_helper<BetsyCompressor>(...)
call_with_variant_args<BetsyCompressor>(...) 
CallableCustomMethodPointer<BetsyCompressor,void>::call(...) 
Callable::callp(...) 
Callable::call<>()
WorkerThreadPool::_process_task(...)
...
PhysicsServer3DWrapMT::_thread_loop()
```

the physics thread was executing tasks and happened to pick up the `BetsyCompressor` task. 

* Internally this task started a loop and is waiting for a condition variable. 
* No other threads are doing anything so this condition variable will never be triggered
* `BetsyCompressor::_thread_loop` will never finish
* `PhysicsServer3DWrapMT` will never execute a physics update
* The process hangs.

I would say either:

* `PhysicsServer3DWrapMT` should not pick up non-physics related tasks
* `BetsyCompressor` should not start a thread loop as part of a task

Tagging @mihe as he has more experience with `PhysicsServer3DWrapMT` than I do and may be able to tell us who is responsible for these two systems.

Edit: Looking at this some more, this seems to be a general problem that `BetsyCompressor`, `PhysicsServer2DWrapMT`, `PhysicsServer3DWrapMT` and `RenderingServerDefault` all have. They use the thread pool to spawn a `_thread_loop` function that seems to last for the duration of the application. That function will then start executing regular tasks and if that happens to execute one of the other global `_thread_loop` functions then the application will deadlock.

@RandomShaper would be my go-to for Godot threading mysteries like these.

